senses.definition: present participle and gerund of murmur

quotes.text: Iron and coal were the magnets that drew railways to this land of lovely valleys and silent mountains—for such it was a century-and-a-half ago, before man blackened the valleys with the smokes of his forges, scarred the green hills with his shafts and waste-heaps, and drove the salmon from the quiet Rhondda and the murmuring Taff.
quotes.reference: 1939 September, D. S. Barrie, “The Railways of South Wales”, in Railway Magazine, page 157:

examples: the murmurings of trees in the wind

quotes.text: Do all things without murmurings and disputings.
quotes.reference: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London: […] Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Philippians 2:14:

quotes.text: When Mrs. Churchill's orders were made known, they caused many secret marvellings and murmurings.
